current_episode.title: Most Replayed Moment: Is Renting Keeping You Poor? What's The Actual Cost Of Home Ownership? David Bach

guest.bio_context: David Bach came out of college in credit card debt with $12,000 owed. He bought his first home by partnering with a best friend, Andrew, splitting a $12,500 down payment on a $250,000 fixer-upper and renting out bedrooms to cover mortgage payments. He wrote The Automatic Millionaire 20 years ago and has spent the last 30 years launching books globally, starting with Oprah.

context.real_quote: It is an absolute freaking myth that people take this extra money that they could have used to buy a house and they're going to put it in the stock market. They don't do that.

pending_qa.q: How quickly can a homeowner sell their property in the current real estate market?
pending_qa.r: The average time from listing to sale is about 47 to 62 days in 2025, including 16 days on the market and 30 to 45 days to close. In hot markets, homes can sell in less than 30 days, and even in slower markets, the process typically takes 1.5 to 3 months.

pending_qa.q: What percentage of retirement savings are held in stocks and retirement accounts nationally?
pending_qa.r: There are $45 trillion dollars now in retirement accounts in America, with 60 to 70% in stocks. Combined with the $34 trillion in home equity, these two wealth sources alone equal approximately $80 trillion.

pending_qa.q: How much interest can be saved using a biweekly mortgage payment plan?
pending_qa.r: By paying a mortgage biweekly instead of monthly, a 30-year mortgage can be paid off five years earlier. Depending on the size of the home, this approach can save between $50,000 to $100,000 just in interest payments.

pending_qa.q: What percentage of net worth does a long-term homeowner typically have in home equity?
pending_qa.r: Over 50% of a homeowner's net worth who has owned their home for 20 years is typically in the equity of their house.

pending_qa.q: What stock market returns have occurred over the past 20 years?
pending_qa.r: The stock market over the last 20 years has averaged over 10% annually. If someone had invested $100,000, it would have grown to $600,000, representing a 600% increase.
